question: What does the study of anatomy primarily focus on?
explanation: Anatomy specifically investigates the physical form and structural relationships of body parts. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why must a nurse study both anatomy and physiology together?

options.A: Hospitals require both subjects for promotion
options.B: It helps in writing long nursing care plans
options.C: Structure dictates how a body part functions
options.D: Physiology is just another name for anatomy

explanation: The physical design of an organ directly determines how it performs its specific role in the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the basic living unit of the human body?
explanation: Cells are recognized as the smallest structural and functional units capable of independent life. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: An organ is best described as a combination of what lower structural levels?
explanation: Organs are formed when two or more distinct tissue types work together to perform complex functions. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: What term describes all the chemical reactions occurring within the body?
explanation: Metabolism encompasses both the breakdown and buildup of chemical compounds in living tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: A patient quickly pulls their hand away from a hot stove. Which life process does this show?
explanation: Responsiveness is the ability of an organism to detect and react to changes in its environment. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: In the standard anatomical position, where do the palms of the hands face?
explanation: Facing the palms forward is a key part of the universal anatomical position used for medical descriptions. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which body plane cuts the body into upper and lower sections?
explanation: A transverse plane creates a horizontal cross-section, splitting the body into superior and inferior parts. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which muscle separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominopelvic cavity?
explanation: The diaphragm is the primary dome-shaped skeletal muscle acting as a physical partition between the chest and abdomen. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of the serous fluid found between membrane layers?

options.A: To reduce friction during organ movement
options.B: To supply oxygen directly to the organs
options.C: To anchor organs tightly to the bone
options.D: To fight off invading bacterial infections

explanation: Serous fluid acts as a lubricant so moving organs like the lungs and heart glide smoothly against cavity walls. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h5)

question: What part of a homeostatic control system detects a stimulus?
explanation: Receptors act as sensors that continuously monitor the internal and external environment for changes. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)

question: How do negative feedback mechanisms protect the human body?

options.A: By speeding up disease progression to finish an infection quickly
options.B: By reversing a directional change back toward a normal set point
options.C: By destroying damaged receptors before they send false signals
options.D: By shutting down all organ systems during times of severe stress

explanation: Negative feedback works to counteract deviations from normal physiological ranges to maintain stability. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)
